title: Incorporating Numerical Variables with Word Vectors to Enhance Predictive Accuracy
description:
I have numerical variables like age, in addition to word vectors generated from sentences. I'm looking for a way to incorporate these numerical variables to improve predictive accuracy.

Is there a method to extract word vectors for each observation?

title: Support for OVA loss
description:
hey there,
 firstly compliment to you for your great work so far. it was really intuitive getting along with the package, and it also works great loading a model from other programming language  and using it. But working with it we discovered a problem.  It appeared we got other results from this package in comparison to the results we got from the FT package in python while using the same trained model. We think the problem could be that the current version of this package isn't supporting the one vs all (ova) loss. 
 
So here comes my issue, could you implement the ova loss while working with already trained models? We would really appreciate it!

Thanks in advance and stay healthy ✌️

title: How to get sentence vectors?
description:
Hello everyone,

I have trained my own fastText model with this package (through `{wordsalad}`) and would now like to obtain "sentence vectors" based on my model for new observations. This package does not implement such a functionality as far as I can see. However, fastText seems to have implemented a function for this: https://github.com/facebookresearch/fastText/blob/a20c0d27cd0ee88a25ea0433b7f03038cd728459/src/fasttext.cc#L490

As far as I can make out, the function to get sentence vectors seems to perform roughly the following steps:
- It calculates the norm of each word vector in a sentence, using the function `norm`.
- It divides each word vector by its norm to normalise it.
- It adds a special end-of-sentence token `</s>`.
- It calculates the average of all normalised word vectors and the end-of-sentence token.

In addition, `{textrecipes}` also seems to provide internal functionality to get a common vector for the aggregate of multiple tokens.

What would be the best way for me to get a "sentence vector". Should this function be exported from the original C++ package here in this package? Do I need to use `{textrecipes}` to get this functionality or should I/must I write my own function?

Many thanks and best regards!

title: Output not saved
description:
Hi. I was using a previous version of fastTextR and now reinstalled the new version of the package updated (I guess in Oct 2022).
Previously, it used to generate ".txt" file and ".bin" files, but with the current version even with the "save_output" option on, it does not generate these two files in the working directory. I tried changing the specification of the directory in multiple different ways but still no luck.

Below I am attaching my code. Can you please help? Thank you!

`PATH_INPUT = "/Users/myproject/output_token_single_file.txt"
PATH_OUT = "/Users/myproject/rt_fst_model"

vecs <- fastTextR::ft_train(file = PATH_INPUT, method = "skipgram",
control = ft_control(learning_rate = 0.02, learn_update = 100, output = PATH_OUT, save_output = TRUE,
word_vec_size = 400, window_size = 5, epoch = 15, min_count = 1, neg = 5,
max_ngram = 2, loss = "hs", nbuckets = 2e+06,
nthreads = 8, t = 1e-04, verbose = 2))`

title: Need an example with data and labels
description:
Hello, I'm a bit confused with the labels, I don't understand how to put them correctly in my data.


I have sample data

```
fu <- function(){
size <- sample(10:30,1)
let <- LETTERS[sample(1:26,size = size,replace = T)]
mu <- make.unique(let,sep = "_")

c(  paste0("__label__",sample(1:2,1))  ,  mu)
}

li <- list()
for(i in 1:20) li[[i]] <- fu()

li2 <- lapply(li ,function(x) paste(x,collapse = " "))

head(li2)
```
the result is
```
[[1]]
[1] "__label__2 Y W Y_1 Y_2 E Z F N E_1 Q"

[[2]]
[1] "__label__1 N A I T D X E M Z F J V I_1 Y Q B J_1 R Y_1 Q_1 C U H R_1 Y_2 D_1 C_1 K"

[[3]]
[1] "__label__1 V F R B E R_1 M I U L Q C D K D_1 M_1 A M_2 A_1 M_3 S R_2 F_1 Z N A_2 E_1 M_4 G"

[[4]]
[1] "__label__2 O K D K_1 C D_1 J L Q F Y N Q_1 A Y_1 F_1 M V D_2"
```

save data

```
way <- "C:\...........\text.txt"
for(i in 1:length(li2))  write.table(x = li2[[i]] , file = way,append = T,col.names = F,row.names = F)
```

train model
```
library("fastTextR")
cntrl <- ft_control(word_vec_size = 10L, learning_rate = 0.1, max_len_ngram = 2L, 
                    min_count = 1L, nbuckets = 100000L, epoch = 5L, nthreads = 4L)
model <- ft_train(file = way, method = "supervised", control = cntrl)
model
```

model have no labels

    443 tokens, 90 words, 0 labels
